head.citation-title: Characterization the carbonation behavior of recycled brick-concrete fines and its pozzolanic reactivity enhancement: The role of red brick fines
head.abstracts: © 2025 Elsevier Ltd.Recycled concrete fines (RCF) commonly contain red brick fines (RBF), yet the effects of such inclusions on carbonation behavior and pozzolanic reactivity remain unclear. The study investigates the carbonation behavior and pozzolanic reactivity enhancement of recycled brick–concrete fines (RBCF) with varied RBF contents. In contrast to conventional RCF, RBF contains reactive silica–alumina components that facilitate the polymerization of silicate species and stimulate the generation of amorphous silica–alumina gels during the carbonation process. Experimental results reveal that RBF incorporation not only alters carbonation product composition but also reduces water demand, enhances later-stage heat release, and significantly improves 28-day compressive strength. A synergistic interface between CaCO3 precipitation and RBF-derived gels was observed, leading to a self-enhancing pozzolanic system. The blend with 40 % RBF exhibited the most balanced performance, demonstrating optimized early–late-stage reactivity. These findings provide new insights into the valorization of mixed construction waste through controlled carbonation and lay the foundation for designing high-performance, low-carbon supplementary cementitious materials.
